bull_bear.body:
- "Under-leveraged" balance sheet; leverage comfortable and "under control"; debt falls off as projects commission and EBITDA kicks in.
- Room for incremental thermal/RE bids without stressing leverage.
- Nabha funded via equity raise INR3,500–4,000 cr + existing debt.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- UNOSUGEN PPC cap recurring (INR171 cr this Q; INR273 cr credit last Q) — appeal-dependent; timing volatility.
- LNG price (Strait of Hormuz / Iran-related) at $16–20 makes RTC merchant uneconomic; domestic gas pooled away from power sector (IOCL force majeure on Qatar gas).
- GBI exhaustion structurally lowers RE incentive income.
- Execution/transmission-line timing for 4 GW RE; MSEDCL land relocation; SECI-12 COD slippage.
- Performance-milestone risk on the new incentive-based ROE.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, granular, candid (e.g. openly corrected an analyst's "3 cargoes" understanding; declined to over-promise on guidance). Comfortable framing one-offs but transparent that carrying-cost income is recurring. Tone: steady, expansion-oriented.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Gas strategy is "demonstrate availability, not necessarily generate" — fixed-cost recovery hinges on availability, so spot/short-term cargoes suffice; PLF deliberately optimized to DISCOM demand. ~5 of the 10 BP/JERA cargoes (from CY27) earmarked for Torrent Power, rest for Torrent Gas.
- The INR186 cr carrying cost is NOT treated as a one-off by mgmt — bulls modelling "clean" EBITDA should not strip it.
- Merchant 603 MW RE may convert to contracted as bids are won — not permanently merchant.
- Batteries on existing hybrid/RTC projects are small; no major config/IRR shift expected near-term.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Net Debt to EBITDA of 2.06x; Net Debt to Equity of 0.56x for FY26", presented under the heading "Comfortable Leverage Provides Headroom to Capitalise on Emerging Opportunities".
- Five-year leverage trend: Net Debt/EBITDA 2.24, 1.97, 2.25, 1.41, 2.06 and Net Debt/Equity 0.80, 0.82, 0.80, 0.40, 0.56 across 21-22 to 25-26.
- Returns trend across 21-22 to 25-26: Return on Capital Employed 10.3%, 14.0%, 11.6%, 12.7%, 10.3% and Return on Networth 14.2%, 19.1%, 14.5%, 18.4%, 12.2%.
- Net worth (including DTL) has risen from Rs 10,289 Crore in 2021-22 to Rs 20,704 Crore in 2025-26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Distribution** (licensed Ahmedabad/Surat + franchises): cash engine; AT&C losses ~2.5% (best-in-class); regulatory gap cut by ~INR800 cr; INR58 cr rooftop-solar incentive; carrying-cost orders recurring.
- **Gas generation**: ~50% tied to own DISCOMs on long-term PPA (fixed-cost recovery on availability); rest merchant. Historic PLF 30–35%.
- **Renewables**: GBI roll-off is the swing factor this quarter.
- **Nabha Power**: EV ~INR6,800 cr, debt ~INR3,400 cr, equity raise INR3,500–4,000 cr planned; 2-part tariff (variable pass-through).

business.body:
- Integrated private-sector utility present "across generation, transmission and distribution", with market capitalisation of "c. Rs 71,330Cr" as on 30th June 2026 and promoter holding of 51.09% (public 48.91%).
- Part of the Torrent Group alongside Torrent Pharmaceuticals and Torrent Gas; the deck says being part of the group "enables significant synergies, provides access to talent and competitive financing".
- "More than c.70% of EBITDA comes from integrated generation and distribution business segment in FY26", with "c.32.8% of operating thermal and c.44.0% of the operating renewable capacity tied to its own distribution business".
- Bhiwandi described as "Country's first of its kind distribution franchisee agreement with MSEDCL" - the first arrangement allowing a private company to manage an area's distribution business.
- Ahmedabad and Surat distribution "received A+ grade, ranking 1st nation wide in the 14th Integrated ratings and rankings for FY25".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Nabha Power - a 1,400 MW (2 x 700) supercritical coal plant at Patiala, Punjab with a 25-year PSPCL PPA set up under Case II Competitive Bidding Guidelines - was acquired with effect from 25.06.2026 and is included in the 30.06.2026 capacity figures.
- [Group asset, not TPL] Torrent Gas Limited, incorporated in FY19, has 17 operating Geographical Areas across 34 districts, 7 states and 1 Union Territory, >17,270 inch-km steel pipeline, >8,100 km MDPE pipeline, >500 CNG stations and more than 2.10 lac PNG domestic connections - these are group, not listed-entity, assets.
- [Fuel security] Amgen has a Fuel Supply Agreement with SECL and Nabha long-term FSAs with SECL and NCL; Anuppur's coal supply is "Arranged by MPPMCL under the SHAKTI Policy of Ministry of Coal".
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- Generation margin compressed by scheduled-maintenance O&M (~INR40 cr) + base-effect of PY provision reversal; UNOSUGEN cap is the headline drag.
- New tariff regime: post-Apr-25 assets earn ROCE with base ROE 13% (up to 15% on milestones) vs old fixed 14%; pre-Apr-25 assets keep old framework but now also earn milestone incentives → effective ROE ~14%→15%.
- Full-year merchant + LNG gains ~INR675 cr on ~1,400 MUs.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- UNOSUGEN: Q2/prior quarter booked a +INR273 cr credit (cap removed in TP's favour); this quarter takes a −INR171 cr provision (cap re-imposed for FY24-25 true-up) — same recurring contest, opposite sign.
- Generation swung to reported EBITDA loss (−INR39 cr) vs prior positive, on the provision + scheduled maintenance + base effect.
- Khavda transmission commissioned this quarter (new vs pipeline prior).
- Coal MP project advanced: PPA signed, BTG/BOP LOA, EC received (milestones newly hit).
- PSP advanced: ESF agreement, civil/E&M LOAs, EC received.
- Nabha acquisition moved from announced to CP-compliance, consolidation now guided for Jun-2026.
- Summer gas: 2 of 3 contracted cargoes received (non-Persian-Gulf source), 3rd due June.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- **No explicit earnings guidance given.** Capex will be "much, much higher" than FY26; declined to confirm 2x.
- 5-year aggregate capex framework confirmed: ~INR80,000 cr (RE INR28,000 cr + Coal INR23,000 cr + PSP INR14,000 cr + ~INR2,000 cr/yr distribution); roughly INR15,000–20,000 cr/yr, back-loaded to years 2–3.
- RE commissioning **1.2–1.4 GW in FY27**.
- **Nabha Power consolidation expected from Jun-2026 (Q1 FY27)** — key item to verify next quarter.
- ROE: new ROCE-based regime expected to improve effective ROE by ~1%/yr if performance milestones met.
outlook.title: Guidance (verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Renewables 4 GW under implementation (~50% wind / 50% solar new builds); incl. SECI-12 (extension applied, COD ~before Mar-27), 367 MW MSEDCL (mostly commissioned; balance delayed by govt land relocation, ~6–9 months), 603 MW merchant (wind-tilted, no battery for now).
- Coal: 1.6 GW MP thermal — PPA with MPPMCL signed, LOA for BTG & BOP issued, EC received.
- PSP: 3 GW pumped storage — ESF agreement with MSEDCL signed, civil/hydro-mech & E&M LOAs issued, EC received.
- Transmission: Khavda commissioned this quarter; Solapur under construction.
- C&I renewables: 860 MW under construction.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- PSP (3 GW) and battery/hybrid/RTC tilt = energy-transition / storage optionality.
- Merchant gas + merchant RE = upside when power deficit/peak pricing returns.
- Parallel licensing — no further development this quarter.
- Active interest in upcoming state thermal bids.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Under-leveraged, balanced integrated utility entering a multi-year ~INR80,000 cr capex super-cycle (RE + coal + PSP + Nabha) funded off a regulated-ROE distribution cash engine; near-term optics muddied by a recurring UNOSUGEN provision and GBI roll-off, but adjusted earnings up 16%.

open.horizon: Expected to be consummated by Q1 FY27
open.item: Acquisition of 100% equity stake and convertible instruments in Nabha Power Limited (1,400 MW supercritical coal-based thermal capacity) from L&T Power Development Limited, fully contracted under long-term PPA with Punjab State Power Corporation Limited.
SECI Tranche XVI wind project (100 MW contracted / 122 MW under installation) in Karnataka via Torrent Solar Power Private Limited, expected commercial operation by December 2026.

MSKVY 2.0 solar project (306 MW contracted / 367 MWp) with MSEDCL in Nashik district, Maharashtra; ~311 MWp commissioned as of 31 March 2026, with PM-KUSUM commissioning deadline extended to 31 March 2027 and an extension petition pending before the Commission.

REMCL RE-RTC Power Project (100 MW contracted / 400.7 MWp combined wind and solar with 5 MW/20 MWh BESS) with South Eastern Railway in Maharashtra via Torrent Solar Power Private Limited, expected commissioning in Q4 FY27.

TPL-D Hybrid Power Project (450 MW contracted / 830 MWp installation, own DISCOM offtaker) in Gujarat via Torrent Saurya Urja 2 Private Limited; Phase 1 expected commercial operation in Q2 FY27, Phase 2 in Q4 FY27.
SECI Tranche XVIII wind project (300 MW), split 175 MW in Gujarat via Torrent Saurya Urja 2 and 125 MW in Maharashtra via Torrent Solar Power, scheduled commissioning in Q3 FY28.

open.horizon: retrospective from Jan 1, 2028 if operations continue beyond Dec 31, 2030
open.item: AMGEN (362 MW coal-based plant) is non-compliant with SOx emission norms; if operations continue beyond the planned closure date (Dec 31, 2030), an environmental compensation charge of Rs 0.40/kWh generated will be imposed retrospectively from January 1, 2028 until the plant ceases operations.
AMGEN must comply with CEA's flexible operation mandate (minimum load operation at 40% MCR) under Phase 4, with compliance deadline of January 2030; a feasibility study has been initiated.

2x800 MW ultra-supercritical coal-based thermal power project at Anuppur, Madhya Pradesh via Newzone India Private Limited, investment of approximately Rs 23,000 Crore; Unit I to be commissioned within 66 months and Unit II within 72 months from PPA execution.

Aggregate regulatory gap of Rs 1,053 Crore (primarily carrying-cost claims) is under dispute at various forums and not accrued in the financial statements; to be accrued when disputes are determined by the appropriate statutory authorities.
SECI Tranche XII wind project (300 MW, Karnataka, via Torrent Saurya Urja 2 Private Limited) has an application pending for extension of its Scheduled Commercial Operation Date.

First FDRE project (250 MW contracted / ~500 MWp wind+solar with 112.5 MW/450 MWh BESS) with the Company's own DISCOM, in Karnataka; Scheduled Commercial Operation Date is 24 months from PPA execution.

1,567 MW of the Company's 2,730 MW operational gas-based capacity is uncontracted and exposed to merchant market conditions; growing coal-based capacity availability and continued renewable growth (declining tariffs) may constrain contracting/dispatch opportunities for this uncontracted capacity.
Solapur transmission project under construction, at an advanced stage of implementation, reinforcing the Company's transmission growth pipeline.
Investing in ~8.4 GW Pumped Storage Hydro pipeline across Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh to support green hydrogen/energy storage growth.
Planning ~7 GWp of additional generation capacity over existing operational capacity, in line with growing energy demand considering data centres and other loads.
Executed long-term LNG procurement agreements with BP and JERA securing ~10 cargoes annually (including for group company) over a 10-year period commencing April 2027.
250 MW Firm and Dispatchable Renewable Energy (FDRE) project secured from own DISCOM at Rs 4.87 per kWh.
Letter of Award secured for 300 MW wind project under SECI's Wind Tranche-XVIII at a tariff of Rs 3.97 per unit.

drhp.business: Torrent Power is an integrated power utility with thermal (coal and gas-based) and renewable (solar and wind) generation, transmission, and distribution operations spanning Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and the UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. risks.note: 1,567 MW of the Company's 2,730 MW operational gas-based capacity is uncontracted and exposed to short-term/merchant conditions; LNG prices are inherently volatile (averaged ~USD 28/MMBtu in FY23, ~USD 11.8/MMBtu in FY26, but spiked to ~USD 20.5/MMBtu in March 2026 amid Middle East tensions), and take-or-pay/use-or-pay/ship-or-pay fuel and regasification contracts could expose the Company to charges under adverse LNG market conditions.
risks.risk: Uncontracted gas-based capacity exposed to merchant market and LNG price volatility

risks.note: The proposed unified/levelised pipeline tariff framework may be unfavourable for plants located closer to the gas source by increasing transportation charges, potentially impacting their competitiveness in merit-order dispatch.
risks.risk: Regulatory change to gas pipeline tariffs (PNGRB 'One Nation, One Grid, One Tariff')

risks.note: AMGEN is non-compliant with SOx emission norms and faces a retrospective environmental compensation charge of Rs 0.40/kWh from January 1, 2028 if it operates beyond its planned December 31, 2030 closure; it must also meet a CEA flexible-operation (minimum load) mandate by January 2030, and is in discussions with the Government of Gujarat over a proposed transfer of part of its ash pond land at Motera for a sports complex.
risks.risk: AMGEN (362 MW coal plant) environmental and regulatory compliance exposure

risks.note: Unrecovered regulatory claims stood at Rs 2,348 Crore (recognised) and a further Rs 1,053 Crore under dispute (not recognised) at year end; in August 2025 the Supreme Court directed DISCOMs to clear existing regulatory assets within four years and capped the regulatory asset at 3% of ARR, tightening the timeline for cash-flow recovery from tariff-related delays.
risks.risk: Regulatory-asset build-up and delayed cost recovery in licensed distribution

risks.note: Growth is constrained by difficulty acquiring suitable land for high-potential wind sites, near-saturated ISTS substation connectivity booked till 2030, and delays in obtaining Right of Use/Right of Way clearances for transmission lines, any of which can cause cost/time overruns and affect scheduled commissioning; operational renewable projects also face penalty risk from stringent scheduling and forecasting rules despite unpredictable weather.
risks.risk: Execution risk in renewable energy pipeline

risks.note: Cybercrime, ransomware and third-party risk are flagged as key concerns; the Company has deployed AI-based EDR, UEM, WAF, Zero Trust Architecture and a Vendor Risk Management system, obtained ISO 27001:2022 certification for IT policies, and carries cyber insurance, indicating this is treated as a material ongoing exposure.

Long Term Debt to Equity increased from 0.46 to 0.67 and Net Debt to EBITDA increased from 1.41 to 2.06 year-on-year due to higher debt drawn to fund incremental capex for under-construction projects; the corresponding EBITDA accretion is only expected to start post-commissioning of these projects, creating an interim leverage/coverage lag.
risks.risk: Rising leverage from debt-funded growth capex ahead of EBITDA accretion
